t: Fixing Our Eyes on God Alone
v: Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the LORD’s house, before the new court;
and he said, “LORD, the God of our fathers, aren’t you God in heaven? Aren’t you ruler over all the kingdoms of the nations? Power and might are in your hand, so that no one is able to withstand you.
Didn’t you, our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel, and give it to the offspring of Abraham your friend forever?
They lived in it, and have built you a sanctuary in it for your name, saying,

‘If evil comes on us—the sword, judgment, pestilence, or famine—we will stand before this house, and before you (for your name is in this house), and cry to you in our affliction, and you will hear and save.’
Now, behold, the children of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom you would not let Israel invade when they came out of the land of Egypt, but they turned away from them, and didn’t destroy them;
behold, how they reward us, to come to cast us out of your possession, which you have given us to inherit.
Our God, will you not judge them? For we have no might against this great company that comes against us. We don’t know what to do, but our eyes are on you.”
b: When King Jehoshaphat faced a vast enemy army, he did not rely on military strategy or human strength. Instead, he gathered the people before the temple and prayed to God. He began by declaring God’s sovereignty: God is the God of heaven and ruler over all the nations, and in his hand are power and might that no one can withstand. This reminds us that the foundation of prayer is not our circumstances, but God’s character and authority.

Jehoshaphat also remembered what God had done in the past, acknowledging that the land was given to the descendants of Abraham. When trouble came, he chose to stand on God’s promises and asked God to fulfill what he had spoken. This is an expression of faith: bringing the challenges of reality before God and connecting them with his word.

The most moving line is this: “We have no power against this great multitude that comes against us. We don’t know what to do, but our eyes are on you.” It is humble surrender, and it is also faith lifted high. When we admit our limits and fix our eyes on God, we can experience his deliverance.
a: Declare God’s sovereignty
In hard times, don’t look first at the circumstances. First affirm that God is the Almighty Lord.
Remember what God has done
Count God’s past grace and promises, and let them build your faith for today.
Look to God alone
Learn, when you feel powerless, to turn your eyes to God and depend on him alone.
q: When I face pressure or challenges, do my eyes usually go first to my circumstances or to God? Am I willing to learn, like Jehoshaphat, to turn my focus back to God’s sovereignty?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, You are the ruler of all nations, and in Your hand are power and might. When I face difficulties and challenges, help me not to depend on myself but to fix my eyes wholly on You. Let me remember Your promises and Your works, knowing that You will surely hear and save. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: My eyes are on God alone, and he will bring deliverance!

t: Made Strong Under God’s Mighty Hand
v: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time,
casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
Be sober and self-controlled. Be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
Withstand him steadfast in your faith, knowing that your brothers who are in the world are undergoing the same sufferings.
But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.
b: Peter reminds us that a spiritual life needs an attitude of humility. When we humble ourselves under God’s mighty hand, we admit that we do not live by our own strength but trust in his sovereignty. God promises that at the proper time he himself will lift us up and accomplish his good purpose.

Our worries grow heavier when we carry them ourselves, but when we cast them on God, we receive his care. He knows our needs and cares about our weakness. This is true rest, because the One who carries our burden is almighty and loving.

At the same time, we must stay alert, because our enemy the devil prowls like a roaring lion, constantly looking for someone to devour. But believers do not fight alone. We can resist him with firm faith, and we know that our brothers and sisters are going through the same trials. In Christ we have companions, and a hope that never fails.

God is the giver of all grace, and he has called us into eternal glory. Even if we suffer for a little while, he himself will make us complete, establish us, and give us strength, until the day we see his face.
a: Humbly submit to God’s hand
Learn to let go of control and place your life in God’s leading.
Cast your worries on God
Don’t carry burdens alone. Practice entrusting everything to the Lord in prayer.
Stay alert and resist the enemy
Face spiritual battle with firm faith, and be victorious through the Lord.
q: Do I still habitually carry my worries on my own? In trials, am I willing to learn humility and submission, and to anchor my faith firmly in God’s promises?
pr: Lord, I am willing to humble myself under Your mighty hand, knowing that Your timing is always best. Help me to cast all my worries on You, and to hold fast to firm faith when the enemy attacks. Thank You that You Yourself will make me complete, establish me, and strengthen me, so that I walk in Your grace and glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I cast my worries on God, and he will strengthen me and give me power to be victorious!

t: Compassion Matters More Than the Plant
v: Then Jonah went out of the city and sat on the east side of the city, and there made himself a booth and sat under it in the shade, until he might see what would become of the city.
The LORD God prepared a vine and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shade over his head to deliver him from his discomfort. So Jonah was exceedingly glad because of the vine.
But God prepared a worm at dawn the next day, and it chewed on the vine so that it withered.

When the sun arose, God prepared a sultry east wind; and the sun beat on Jonah’s head, so that he was faint and requested for himself that he might die. He said, “It is better for me to die than to live.”
God said to Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry about the vine?” He said, “I am right to be angry, even to death.”
The LORD said, “You have been concerned for the vine, for which you have not labored, neither made it grow; which came up in a night and perished in a night.

Shouldn’t I be concerned for Nineveh, that great city, in which are more than one hundred twenty thousand persons who can’t discern between their right hand and their left hand, and also many animals?”
b: Jonah sat outside the city, waiting to see whether God would carry out judgment. But God caused a vine to spring up, comforting his body, and then took it away. Through this he let Jonah see that he cared more about a plant than about God’s compassion for the people. God’s purpose was not to torment him, but to awaken him: human compassion is limited, while God’s compassion is wide enough to embrace everything.

Jonah’s anger exposed a self-centered heart that used justice for selfish ends. He would rather see judgment carried out than see people repent and be saved. God made a simple comparison: you care about a plant that you did not even plant, so how much more should I care about the city I have made, whose people cry out for mercy? This reminds us that faith is not only holding to doctrine, but letting compassion and obedience take shape in daily life.

God not only showed his sovereignty, he was also teaching his disciple an ethic of life: let the Lord’s compassion be the first measure of our judgments and actions. When we learn to lay down self-righteousness and take on the heart of Jesus, we can live out a witness that is both just and merciful in prayer, intercession, and service, and help build a community that welcomes repentance and restoration.
a: Examine my motives
When I speak up for justice, I should ask myself whether it is for God’s glory or just to prove myself right.
Put compassion first
When you meet someone in trouble, respond first with sympathy and help, then guide with truth, so that rescue comes before condemnation.
Obey God’s teaching
Notice the moments when God reminds you through small things, and let him gently reshape your heart.
q: Do I love being “right” more than I love people being saved? If God asked me today to lay down my anger, how would I respond?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, forgive me for so often putting myself at the center. Give me a compassionate heart like Jesus, so that I may intercede for the lost and act in love within the truth. Help me not to measure justice by small gains, but to take Your compassion as the measure of my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: The Lord’s compassion is greater than my opinions, and I want to love and restore people with his heart.

t: Trusting the Lord Who Rules the Storm
v: On that day, when evening had come, he said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side.”
Leaving the multitude, they took him with them, even as he was, in the boat. Other small boats were also with him.
A big wind storm arose, and the waves beat into the boat, so much that the boat was already filled.
He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion; and they woke him up and asked him, “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?”
He awoke and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased and there was a great calm.
He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”
They were greatly afraid and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
b: This passage vividly shows how the disciples reacted in a crisis, and the authority of Jesus. The storm struck suddenly, and the boat was nearly swallowed by the waves. The disciples’ fear was a natural human reaction. Yet Jesus slept peacefully in the stern, showing that he trusted the Father completely and was in control of every circumstance.

When the disciples cried out in panic, “Don’t you care that we are dying?”, Jesus rose and calmed the storm with a single word. He did not only quiet the elements, he also challenged their hearts: “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?” The real storm was not only on the sea, but within the disciples.

This reminds us that following Jesus does not mean we will never meet storms, but that he goes with us in the same boat. Faith is not denying the crisis. It is recognizing his authority in the crisis and resting in his presence. When we choose to rely on him, we can experience the wonderful grace of “a great calm.”
a: Learn to look to the Lord in the storm
We cannot control our circumstances, but Jesus rules over all, and faith keeps us from being drowned by fear.
Call on him in prayer
When crisis comes, our first response should not be complaint but turning to Jesus and calling on him to save.
Be sure of his presence
However big the waves, he is in the boat. His presence is the foundation of our peace.
q: In the storms of my life, am I first swallowed by fear, or do I choose to come to Jesus first?
pr: Lord Jesus, thank You for being in my boat. Help me not to be gripped by fear in the storm, but to look to You alone. Teach me, in times of trouble, to depend on You and call on You, and to believe that Your presence will bring peace. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: The storm cannot defeat me, because the Lord Jesus is with me!

t: Jesus, Our Brother and Savior
v: You made him a little lower than the angels. You crowned him with glory and honor.
You have put all things in subjection under his feet.” For in that he subjected all things to him, he left nothing that is not subject to him. But now we don’t yet see all things subjected to him.
But we see him who has been made a little lower than the angels, Jesus, because of the suffering of death crowned with glory and honor, that by the grace of God he should taste of death for everyone.
For it became him, for whom are all things and through whom are all things, in bringing many children to glory, to make the author of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
For both he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one, for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brothers,
saying, “I will declare your name to my brothers. Among the congregation I will sing your praise.”
Again, “I will put my trust in him.” Again, “Behold, here I am with the children whom God has given me.”

Since then the children have shared in flesh and blood, he also himself in the same way partook of the same, that through death he might bring to nothing him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,
and might deliver all of them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.
b: Jesus Christ willingly humbled himself, becoming for a little while lower than the angels, and because of the suffering of death he was crowned with glory and honor. He did this not for himself but for us, willingly tasting death so that we might have life and hope. His suffering was no accident, but part of God’s wise plan, by which the author of our salvation was made perfect through suffering.

Even more wonderful, he calls us his brothers and sisters and is not ashamed of us. He sings praise to God in the congregation and regards us as children of the same family. This close relationship shows our position in him: we are no longer outsiders, but members of God’s household.

Because he took on flesh and blood, he entered into our weakness and limitations, and finally, through death on the cross, he completely destroyed the power of the devil. From now on, death is no longer our chain, because Jesus has set free those who all their lives were held in bondage by the fear of death. We can now live boldly and without fear, with the hope of eternal life.
a: Reflect on Jesus’ humility and glory
He humbled himself and suffered for us, and now he is glorified. Let us learn to follow his pattern of humble obedience.
Live out your identity as God’s child
Do not shrink back in feelings of inferiority or fear, but live in faith and dignity, in the glory of being called his brother or sister.
Overcome the fear of death
Because Jesus has broken the power of death, we are no longer slaves but free people, able to face the future with courage.
q: Is there any area of my life still held captive by the fear of failure, loss, or death? Am I willing to receive by faith the truth that Jesus has already won the victory?
pr: Lord Jesus, thank You for humbling Yourself to become human, entering into my weakness, suffering for me, and defeating death. Help me always to remember that I am Your brother and Your child, and that I am no longer ruled by fear. May I live boldly and freely in the glory of being God’s child, through Your victory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Jesus has conquered death, and I am no longer a slave to fear!

t: Wise Reminders and True Contentment
v: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
Whoever tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit. He who looks after his master shall be honored.
Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man.
Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.
The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but man is refined by his praise.
Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.
Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds,
for riches are not forever, nor does the crown endure to all generations.
The hay is removed, and the new growth appears, the grasses of the hills are gathered in.
The lambs are for your clothing, and the goats are the price of a field.
There will be plenty of goats’ milk for your food, for your family’s food, and for the nourishment of your servant girls.
b: This passage of proverbs gives us wisdom in many directions. First, people need to encourage one another. Like iron sharpening iron, the reminders and shaping of friends make a life sharper and more valuable. At the same time, those who serve faithfully will be rewarded, because God values our faithfulness.

The writer also points out that a heart that chases what the eyes desire will never be satisfied, just as Sheol is never satisfied. The real test comes not only from circumstances but from how a person handles praise and recognition, which reveal what is truly in the heart. A fool, even when severely disciplined, cannot leave his foolishness behind if his heart does not change.

Finally, wisdom calls us to diligently manage what God has entrusted to us, not by merely piling up wealth or status, but by knowing how to keep working and guard faithfully. Riches and crowns do not last, but diligence and faithfulness bring lasting provision and contentment. The daily provision God gives is the true source of security and joy.
a: Encourage and remind one another
Learn to interact with fellow believers and not reject advice or reminders, for sharpening one another makes life more mature and strong.
Be alert to desire and praise
Do not let the greed of the eyes or the praise of others become a trap, but keep your focus on God’s view.
Diligently manage what God has entrusted
Do not rely on fleeting wealth or position, but faithfully carry out the responsibilities God gave you, and be content with his provision.
q: Is there any place in my life still held captive by the desires of my eyes or by the praise of others? Am I faithfully managing the people and things God has entrusted to me?
pr: Lord, thank You for reminding me that the value of life lies not in passing wealth but in faithfulness and wise stewardship. Help me to receive the reminders and sharpening of others, not to chase empty satisfaction, but to rely wholly on Your provision and live within Your will. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I do not chase empty satisfaction. I diligently and faithfully manage what God has entrusted to me!

t: Strengthened by Grace to Fight the Good Fight
v: I thank him who enabled me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he counted me faithful, appointing me to service,
although I used to be a blasphemer, a persecutor, and insolent. However, I obtained mercy because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
The grace of our Lord abounded exceedingly with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
The saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief.
However, for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first, Jesus Christ might display all his patience for an example of those who were going to believe in him for eternal life.
Now to the King eternal, immortal, invisible, to God who alone is wise, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
I commit this instruction to you, my child Timothy, according to the prophecies which were given to you before, that by them you may wage the good warfare,
holding faith and a good conscience, which some having thrust away made a shipwreck concerning the faith,
of whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I delivered to Satan that they might be taught not to blaspheme.
b: Here Paul gives his own life as a testimony. He admits that he was once a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an insolent man, yet through God’s mercy and grace he went from being the chief of sinners to an apostle who testifies to the Lord’s grace. This reminds us that no one is worthy to serve God by his own deeds. Everything comes from God’s grace and choosing.

He stresses that “Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners,” and uses himself as proof of how long, wide, and deep God’s patience and mercy are. This shows us that no one is too far gone to be changed by God. It is precisely because we are unworthy that the riches of God’s grace shine all the more.

Paul also urges Timothy to “wage the good warfare,” and the secret is holding faith and a good conscience. Faith keeps a person standing firm in Christ, and conscience is the Holy Spirit’s reminder within us. If conscience is lost, faith becomes like a shipwreck, losing its direction.
a: Remember God’s grace and mercy
Whatever our past, we can serve God today only because of his mercy, so we should always keep a thankful heart.
Live out faith and love
True faith always brings forth acts of love, and this is the testimony of God’s grace in our lives.
Hold on to faith and conscience
Let faith guide our direction, and let a clean conscience keep us from drifting away from the truth.
q: Do I still often remember the grace God has shown me? In my life and service, am I living out faith and a good conscience?
pr: Lord, thank You for showing me mercy while I was still a sinner and for choosing me to serve You. Help me always to remember Your grace, strengthen my faith, and keep my conscience clean, so that I can fight the good fight until I see Your face. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am strong by God’s grace. I hold on to faith and a good conscience, and I will boldly fight the good fight!

t: Meeting the God of Compassion and Grace
v: He chiseled two tablets of stone like the first; then Moses rose up early in the morning, and went up to Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, and took in his hand two stone tablets.
The LORD descended in the cloud, and stood with him there, and proclaimed the LORD’s name.
The LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, “The LORD! The LORD, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth,

keeping loving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity and disobedience and sin; and who will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, and on the children’s children, on the third and on the fourth generation.”
Moses hurried and bowed his head toward the earth, and worshiped.

He said, “If now I have found favor in your sight, Lord, please let the Lord go among us, even though this is a stiff-necked people; pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us for your inheritance.”

He said, “Behold, I make a covenant: before all your people I will do marvels, such as have not been worked in all the earth, nor in any nation; and all the people among whom you are shall see the work of the LORD; for it is an awesome thing that I do with you.
b: This passage comes after the golden calf incident, when the people had just sinned greatly against God by their rebellion. Moses went up Mount Sinai again with new tablets, and God descended in the cloud and revealed his character to his people once more. Here God proclaims himself “a merciful and gracious God.” His love and forgiveness go far beyond what we can imagine; he is willing to forgive rebellion and to keep his loving kindness for thousands of generations.

Yet God’s love is not permissiveness. He is also just, and does not clear the guilty, and the consequences of sin remain. This reminds us that God’s grace is not cheap; it calls us to genuine repentance and to walk with him again in covenant.

Moses responded by bowing to the ground, worshiping, and interceding for the people, asking for God’s presence and forgiveness. He understood that if Israel lost God’s presence, they would lose everything. God’s answer was not only forgiveness, but a promise to do marvels before all the people, so that the nations would see his work.
a: Know God’s character
God is a God of love and grace, and also a God of justice. This lets us draw near to him with reverence, neither taking his love lightly nor ignoring his holiness.
Learn Moses’ heart
Moses quickly bowed down and interceded for the people, an example of worship and intercession. We too should pray for our families, churches, and nations, asking that God’s presence not leave us.
Seek God’s presence
More than blessings and gifts, what matters most is that God walks with us. Only with him present do we have true security and strength.
q: In my life, do I seek God’s blessings more, or God’s presence? When I fail, do I believe God still has compassion and grace and is willing to receive me?
pr: Lord, thank You for showing me that You are a God of compassion and grace. Forgive my sins, so that I no longer have a stiff neck, and help me to seek Your presence always. May my life testify to Your marvelous works, so that others may see Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will follow closely the God of compassion and grace, and his presence is my greatest security!

t: Showing Kindness for Jonathan’s Sake
v: David said, “Is there yet any who is left of Saul’s house, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?”
There was of Saul’s house a servant whose name was Ziba, and they called him to David; and the king said to him, “Are you Ziba?” He said, “I am your servant.”
The king said, “Is there not yet any of Saul’s house, that I may show the kindness of God to him?” Ziba said to the king, “Jonathan still has a son, who is lame in his feet.”
The king said to him, “Where is he?” Ziba said to the king, “Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo Debar.”
Then King David sent and brought him out of the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo Debar.
Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, fell on his face, and showed respect. David said, “Mephibosheth?” He answered, “Behold, your servant!”

David said to him, “Don’t be afraid, for I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father’s sake, and will restore to you all the land of Saul your father. You will eat bread at my table continually.”
So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, for he ate continually at the king’s table. He was lame in both his feet.
b: This story records David’s kindness to Jonathan’s descendants. By the customs of royal succession, David had reason to wipe out Saul’s family to protect his own position, but he chose another path. He did not hold on to old hatreds. Instead, because of his covenant with Jonathan, he showed kindness to Mephibosheth.

Mephibosheth was a disabled and forgotten man, living in the remote place of Lo Debar, a name that even carries a sense of shame. Yet David brought him from that lowly place back to Jerusalem, restored the inheritance he had lost, and honored him by letting him “eat continually at the king’s table.” This was not only practical provision, but the restoration of an identity.

This passage lets us see God’s grace. Because of his covenant with Christ, he does not treat us according to our failures. Instead he receives us, restores our identity, and makes us his children, so that we may enjoy intimate fellowship at his table continually.
a: Receive God’s grace
However weak or broken we have been, God is still willing to receive us, because he remembers his covenant with Christ and brings us to his table.
Learn to show kindness
Like David, treat people not by their merit or conditions, but choose to treat them with kindness because of love and covenant.
Live out your restored identity
Do not live in shame and inferiority, for God has restored our identity and given us honor and standing in him.
q: Am I still living in shame because of my flaws or my past? Or am I willing to believe that God has restored my identity so that I may sit at his table continually?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for receiving me for Jesus Christ’s sake. Even though I am weak and have failed, You brought me to Your table and made me Your child. Help me also to treat others with kindness, and to live out the honored identity I have been restored to in Christ. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God receives me for Christ’s sake, and I will enjoy his grace at his table continually!

t: All That God Made Is Very Good
v: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
God saw the light, and saw that it was good. God divided the light from the darkness.
God called the light “day”, and the darkness he called “night”. There was evening and there was morning, the first day.
God said, “Let there be an expanse in the middle of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.”
God made the expanse, and divided the waters which were under the expanse from the waters which were above the expanse; and it was so.
God called the expanse “sky”. There was evening and there was morning, a second day.
God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning, a sixth day.
b: The opening of Genesis declares the origin of the universe: not by chance, but by God’s own creating hand. Though the earth was at first formless and empty, God’s Spirit hovered over the waters, and his word brought order, light, and life. This reminds us that in the darkness and chaos of life, only God’s word can bring true change and a new beginning.

When God looked at his creation, he called it “good,” and even “very good.” This shows God’s delight and satisfaction in the work of his hands. We too are his creation, valuable in his eyes, not an accident but made with his heart and purpose.

God not only created the heavens and the earth, he also set up order: light and darkness, day and night, earth and sky. This order not only keeps nature running, it also reminds us that we need God to separate and define things in our lives, so that we do not live in chaos but experience abundance within his order.
a: Seek God’s word in the midst of chaos
When life seems empty or dark, choose to return to God’s word and let him bring light and direction.
Accept your value in God’s eyes
Remember that God sees us as his “very good” creation. Stop being bound by inferiority or self-rejection, and live out an identity that pleases God.
Live according to God’s order
Learn to follow God’s boundaries and principles in daily life, and let his order lead us into peace and abundance.
q: When my life falls into chaos or emptiness, do I let God’s word and his Spirit move over it? Do I believe that I am a “very good” creation in God’s eyes?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for creating the heavens and the earth in the beginning, and for creating me. Though my life is sometimes chaotic and dark, Your word brings light and order. Help me to live in Your will and order, and to accept that You see me as very good. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am God’s “very good” creation, and his light will shine in my life!

t: Building Your Life on a Solid Foundation
v: “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine and does them, I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on the rock.
The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house; and it didn’t fall, for it was founded on the rock.
Everyone who hears these words of mine and doesn’t do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house; and it fell—and its fall was great.”
b: Jesus uses the picture of building a house to remind us that the stability of life depends on its foundation. The wise man is not one who only hears the word, but one who acts on it, and so even when the storm comes, his house still stands. True faith is always accompanied by obedient action, because the foundation of rock is God’s word and his truth.

By contrast, the one who does not act is like a man who builds his house on sand. It may look secure for a while, but when trials come the weakness of the foundation is revealed, and the house collapses completely. Jesus reminds us that storms are unavoidable, but what decides the outcome is whether we have built our lives on his word.

This passage is not only a warning, but an invitation. God longs for us to take his word as a practical guide for action and to build our lives on a foundation that can never be shaken, so that we can stand firm in times of trouble.
a: Be rooted in God’s word
Do not only listen to the word, but practice it every day, applying God’s truth in every area of life.
Hold on to obedience in trials
When the wind and rain beat, don’t rely on emotions or circumstances, but on obeying God’s word, and experience a stable life.
Examine the foundation of my life
Honestly ask yourself: are my choices and values built on what people think, or on God’s unchanging word?
q: Is the house of my life built on rock or on sand? In difficult times, do I still steadfastly obey God’s word?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that Your word is the rock of my life. Help me not only to hear but to obey and act, so that my life can stand firm in any storm. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will build my life on God’s word, and the storms will not make me fall!

t: Setting Up Spiritual Memorials
v: When all the nation had completely crossed over the Jordan, the LORD spoke to Joshua, saying,
“Take twelve men out of the people, a man out of every tribe,

and command them, saying, ‘Take from out of the middle of the Jordan, out of the place where the priests’ feet stood firm, twelve stones, carry them over with you, and lay them down in the place where you’ll camp tonight.’”
Then Joshua called the twelve men whom he had prepared of the children of Israel, a man out of every tribe.

Joshua said to them, “Cross before the ark of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan, and each of you pick up a stone and put it on your shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel;
that this may be a sign among you, that when your children ask in the future, saying, ‘What do you mean by these stones?’

then you shall tell them, ‘Because the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the LORD’s covenant. When it crossed over the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. These stones shall be for a memorial to the children of Israel forever.’”

The children of Israel did as Joshua commanded, and took up twelve stones out of the middle of the Jordan, as the LORD spoke to Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel. They carried them over with them to the place where they camped, and laid them down there.
b: Israel’s crossing of the Jordan was not just a miraculous river crossing, but a moment of covenant and remembrance. God told each tribe to take a stone and set it up as a permanent sign, so that later generations would know it as a witness to God’s deliverance. This reminds us that God’s works need to be recorded and handed down, becoming milestones in the history of faith.

These stones were a witness to God’s power, faithfulness, and presence. They also reminded the people that their standing now was not by their own strength but by what God had done. In the same way, we need spiritual markers in our lives to help us and our descendants remember how God led us through hardship.

When children ask, “What do these stones mean?”, parents have a chance to tell of God’s grace. God wants our faith to be not only a personal experience, but a testimony for the community and for generations, so that more people see his glory.
a: Record what God has done
Use writing, a prayer journal, or testimony to keep the moments of God’s grace in your life.
Set up a testimony for your family
Share stories of God’s grace at home, and let faith be passed down from generation to generation.
Make your life a marker
Let your words and actions witness to God, so that people come to know his faithfulness through you.
q: What “stones” does God want me to set up in my life, so that I and my descendants will always remember his grace?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for the deliverance and leading You have given me in the past. Help me to remember Your grace and to set up testimonies in my family, church, and daily life, so that future generations may come to know Your faithfulness through the stories I share. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will remember what God has done, set up a testimony with my life, and proclaim his faithfulness from generation to generation!

t: Tears of Reconciliation and a Testimony of Grace
v: Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
You shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. You shall hurry and bring my father down here.”
He fell on his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
He kissed all his brothers, and wept on them. After that his brothers talked with him.
The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.
He gave each one of them changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.
He sent the following to his father: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provision for his father by the way.
So he sent his brothers away, and they departed. He said to them, “See that you don’t quarrel on the way.”
They went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.
They told him, saying, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” His heart fainted, for he didn’t believe them.
They told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them. When he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob, their father, revived.
b: When Joseph met his brothers again, he did not begin with rebuke but with tears and embraces. His weeping was the overflow of real forgiveness, and a sign that a broken relationship was being healed. This reminds us that true reconciliation does not come through self-defense, but through love and grace.

He told his brothers not to quarrel on the way, because past guilt can easily become an excuse for blaming one another. But in God’s plan, every experience was turned into blessing. Joseph understood what God was doing behind the scenes, so he urged his brothers to let go of strife and focus on the joy of being reunited with their father.

When Jacob heard the news, at first his heart fainted because he did not believe. But when he saw the evidence, his spirit revived. This tells us that God’s works should be made known not only in our own lives, but also become a testimony that brings comfort and hope to others.
a: Choose grace instead of blame
When facing those who have hurt us, don’t rush to judge, but let love bring reconciliation.
Let go of strife and focus on God’s plan
Don’t let past mistakes become today’s burden. Believe that God can turn everything around.
Strengthen others with your testimony
Share what God has done in your life, so that others hear and are revived and given hope.
q: Am I still holding on to past hurts or quarrels? Can I, like Joseph, bring reconciliation and hope through love and testimony?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for the wonderful turnarounds You have worked in my life. Give me a heart willing to forgive, so that I no longer live in strife and blame, but become a channel of grace and testimony. Let me be reconciled with others, and let my life become a sign that revives the hearts of others. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will live out a testimony with love and grace, and become a vessel of reconciliation and hope!

t: Children Blessed in Christ
v: having predestined us for adoption as children through Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his desire,
to the praise of the glory of his grace, by which he freely gave us favor in the Beloved.
In him we have our redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace
b: This passage reveals our glorious identity and position in Christ. God did not choose us because of our good deeds, but because of his love and purpose, he was pleased to make us his children. It is a free gift of grace, and it gives us a secure assurance of who we are.

In the Beloved, we are not only called God’s children, but are redeemed and forgiven. The precious blood of Jesus paid the price for us and opened the way to freedom and new life. This grace is rich, beyond what we can imagine, so that we can live all our lives in thanksgiving and praise.

Therefore, our lives are not for ourselves, but for the praise of the glory of his grace. When we live out our identity as God’s children, we naturally become a witness to the world, so that people see his love and salvation.
a: Establish your identity
Remind yourself often that you are God’s beloved child, not shaken by circumstances or what others say.
Live in forgiveness
No longer be bound by guilt, but live freely through the precious blood of Christ.
Praise his grace
Thank God every day for his grace, and show his glory to others through your life.
q: Am I living today like a beloved, forgiven child of God? How can I give glory to God in my daily life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for choosing me, loving me, and adopting me as Your child through Jesus Christ. Help me always to remember this grace and to live in forgiveness and freedom, so that my life is full of thanksgiving and praise, glorifying Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am God’s beloved child, blessed and forgiven in Christ, to the praise of the glory of his grace!

t: Washed Clean by the Blood of the Lamb
v: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no man could count, out of every nation and of all tribes, peoples, and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands.
They cried with a loud voice, saying, “Salvation be to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!”
One of the elders answered, saying to me, “These who are arrayed in the white robes, who are they, and where did they come from?”
I told him, “My lord, you know.” He said to me, “These are those who came out of the great suffering. They washed their robes and made them white in the Lamb’s blood.
Therefore they are before the throne of God, and they serve him day and night in his temple. He who sits on the throne will spread his tabernacle over them.
They will never be hungry or thirsty any more. The sun won’t beat on them, nor any heat;
for the Lamb who is in the middle of the throne shepherds them and leads them to springs of life-giving waters. And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.”
b: This is a vision of glory in heaven, and the final hope of God’s people. The countless crowd in white robes symbolizes those redeemed in Christ. They stand before God not through their own righteousness, but because they have been washed clean by the precious blood of the Lamb. The white robes represent a life completely forgiven and cleansed.

They are people who came out of great suffering. This shows that the path of faith is not without hardship, yet everyone who holds fast and trusts in Christ will finally enter the rest of glory. The Lamb who shed his blood for us now becomes the Shepherd who tends us, leading us to springs of living water and healing all our wounds.

God’s tabernacle covers his people. There will be no more hunger, no more thirst, no more scorching heat, and no more tears. This is the picture of eternal rest, and the ending and comfort of everyone who belongs to him.
a: Remember the cost of salvation
Often reflect on the forgiveness and cleansing the Lamb’s blood has brought, and do not let the accusation of sin steal your peace.
Hold on to faith to the end
In life’s hardships and challenges, rely on Jesus, for he has already won the victory for us.
Hope for eternal glory
Do not be crushed by the sufferings of this life, but look to the glory of the Lamb in heaven and to everlasting rest.
q: Am I still trying to make my life clean through my own efforts? Or do I trust in the blood of the Lamb and live in forgiveness and peace?
pr: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You that Your precious blood has washed me clean, so that I stand spotless before the Heavenly Father. When I go through suffering, make me steadfast and keep my faith until I see You face to face. Let me live out the joy and hope of redemption here on earth. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: The blood of the Lamb has washed me clean, I am no longer condemned, and I will serve the Lord forever until I see his glorious face!

t: The Power of the Gospel in Persecution
v: They stoned Stephen as he called out, saying, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit!”
He kneeled down and cried with a loud voice, “Lord, don’t hold this sin against them!” When he had said this, he fell asleep.

Saul was consenting to his death. A great persecution arose against the assembly which was in Jerusalem in that day. They were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except for the apostles.
Devout men buried Stephen and lamented greatly over him.
But Saul ravaged the assembly, entering into every house and dragged both men and women off to prison.
Therefore those who were scattered abroad went around preaching the word.
Philip went down to the city of Samaria and proclaimed to them the Christ.
The multitudes listened with one accord to the things that were spoken by Philip when they heard and saw the signs which he did.
For unclean spirits came out of many of those who had them. They came out, crying with a loud voice. Many who had been paralyzed and lame were healed.
There was great joy in that city.
b: Stephen was the first martyr in the history of the church, and even as he died he responded to his persecutors with love, asking the Lord to forgive them. This forgiveness, born of the Holy Spirit, became a spark for the gospel, burning even brighter in persecution. What looked like a tragedy was in fact a turning point by which God advanced the spread of the gospel.

When persecution came, the disciples were scattered, but they did not stay silent or retreat. Instead they “went around preaching the word.” God turned persecution into a push for the gospel, so that the footsteps of salvation crossed borders into Samaria. When Philip proclaimed Christ, signs followed, people were set free and healed, and the city was filled with joy.
This reminds us that even in difficult circumstances, God is still in control. Persecution cannot extinguish faith, but rather purifies the church and spreads the gospel more widely.
a: Choose love in adversity
Learn from Stephen’s example, replacing resentment with forgiveness, and let love be your witness.
See God’s bigger plan
Even in persecution or setbacks, believe that God can turn them into opportunities for the gospel.
Be a messenger of joy
In hard times, keep proclaiming Christ, so that the lives of others are filled with joy because of you.
q: Am I faithful even in difficulty? Am I willing to let God use adversity as a way for the gospel to go forward?
pr: Lord, thank You for letting me see Stephen’s testimony. Give me courage and faith, so that even in affliction I do not lose a heart of love. Make my life a vessel of the gospel, so that Your glory may be seen wherever I go. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Persecution cannot put out faith. I will proclaim Christ in hard times, and the city will be filled with joy!

t: A Household United in Christ
v: that you were at that time separate from Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of the promise, having no hope and without God in the world.
But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off are made near in the blood of Christ.
For he is our peace, who made both one, and broke down the middle wall of separation,
having abolished in his flesh the hostility, the law of commandments contained in ordinances, that he might create in himself one new man of the two, making peace,
and might reconcile them both in one body to God through the cross, having killed the hostility through it.
He came and preached peace to you who were far off and to those who were near.
For through him we both have our access in one Spirit to the Father.
So then you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and of the household of God,
being built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus himself being the chief cornerstone;
in whom the whole building, fitted together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord;
in whom you also are built together for a habitation of God in the Spirit.
b: In this passage Paul reveals the great mystery of the gospel: through Christ, all who were far from God can be brought near again. In the past there was a divide between Gentiles and Israel, a “dividing wall” that stood for law, prejudice, and human separation. But Christ removed all of that on the cross, so that people once estranged from one another could be made one in him.

This unity is not only reconciliation between people, but reconciliation between people and God. Jesus opened the way to the Father by his blood, so that we are moved by one Spirit and enter the Father’s presence. Now we are no longer lonely strangers, but members of God’s household, built up as God’s temple in which the Holy Spirit dwells.
The true church is not a building, but every life joined to Christ. When we love and build one another up, we show the glory of the Prince of Peace.
a: Remember the Lord’s grace
Think of how you were once far from God and are now brought near by the blood of Christ, and keep a thankful heart.
Tear down dividing walls
In family, church, and relationships, learn to forgive and accept, so that the Lord’s peace may come.
Live as a spiritual household
Connect with fellow believers as members of one body, and let the Holy Spirit’s presence fill the community.
q: Am I still separated from certain people today? Which “walls” am I willing to let Christ’s love tear down?
pr: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You for tearing down the dividing wall with the love of the cross, so that I am no longer a stranger but a member of God’s household. Help me to live out a life of unity and peace, and let my heart and the church become a dwelling place for the Holy Spirit. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Christ is my peace. In him I am reconciled with God and united with others, and I become a dwelling place of God’s presence!

t: God Hears Prayers Prayed in Tears
v: In those days Hezekiah was sick and near death. Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him, and said to him, “The LORD says, ‘Set your house in order, for you will die, and not live.’”
Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,
and said, “Remember now, LORD, I beg you, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in your sight.” Then Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then the LORD’s word came to Isaiah, saying,
“Go, and tell Hezekiah, ‘The LORD, the God of David your father, says, “I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.
I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.
b: When Hezekiah faced the announcement of death, he did not argue or despair. He turned his face to the wall and poured out his heart to God. His prayer was not an empty form on his lips, but came from a real, broken, weeping heart. God saw his tears and heard his cry, and so he changed what had been decreed, adding fifteen years to his life and promising to protect his city.

This passage shows us that God is not a cold judge, but a Father who hears prayer and has compassion for the human heart. When we turn to him at our limits, God can make the “impossible” possible and open a path of life in despair. He not only answers prayer, but values the honest, wholehearted heart that truly seeks him as we pray.
a: Turn to God in hardship
Don’t run away or complain. Learn from Hezekiah to “turn your face to the wall” and face God alone.
Pray sincerely, not formally
God does not look at the outward words of a prayer, but at a heart willing to weep honestly before him.
Believe God can change destinies
Even when everything seems beyond recovery, God still has the authority to turn a life around and renew our days.
q: The last time I “turned my face to the wall” to pray, was it out of despair or out of trust? Do I believe God still hears?
pr: Lord, thank You for hearing prayers prayed in tears. When I face my limits, help me not to run away but to turn to You alone. Renew my heart, so that I may honestly, wholeheartedly, and sincerely seek Your will. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God hears my prayer and sees my tears, and he will do wonders for me!

t: The Gospel of the Kingdom Brings Healing
v: Jesus went about in all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

The report about him went out into all Syria. They brought to him all who were sick, afflicted with various diseases and torments, possessed with demons, epileptics, and paralytics; and he healed them.
Great multitudes from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and from beyond the Jordan followed him.
b: Jesus’ ministry was salvation for the whole person. He not only taught truth and preached the gospel of the Kingdom, but also healed people of every kind of sickness in body, mind, and spirit. The “gospel of the Kingdom” he preached is not only about heaven in the future, but about the reality of God’s Kingdom coming to earth now: when people meet Jesus and receive his word, they experience freedom, restoration, and renewal.

Jesus traveled everywhere, regardless of rich or poor, high or low. He entered the synagogues to teach, and walked among the crowds to heal. He cared about people’s spiritual condition and had compassion on their physical pain. Everyone who came to him with a need, whether sickness, pain, demon possession, or paralysis, was healed, because he has not only power but a heart of compassion.
This is the heart of the gospel: when God’s Kingdom comes, people are restored, lives are turned around, the broken are healed, and the hopeless receive hope.
a: Let the Lord reign in your life
The gospel of the Kingdom is not only knowledge, but an invitation for Jesus to be King in my heart and rule over every area.
Bring people to the Lord
Like those people, bring those in need to Jesus, because he can heal and set free.
Proclaim a gospel that brings healing
Don’t only speak a message, but live out the power of the gospel, so that people see God’s love and grace.
q: Do I only want to be healed and forget to make Jesus the Lord of my life? Whom am I willing to “lead” to Jesus?
pr: Lord Jesus, thank You for going among the people and bringing the gospel of the Kingdom into every life in need. Please also heal the sicknesses of my soul and restore my faith and hope, so that I become a vessel to bring people to know You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: The gospel of the Kingdom has come to me, and Jesus is my complete healing and salvation!

t: The True Witness of Christ’s Resurrection
v: For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.
Then he appeared to over five hundred brothers at once, most of whom remain until now, but some have also fallen asleep.
Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles,
and last of all, as to the child born at the wrong time, he appeared to me also.
b: In this passage Paul proclaims the core truth of the gospel: Jesus Christ died for our sins, and was raised from the dead on the third day according to the Scriptures. This is not a religious theory, but a historical fact. Jesus’ death brings forgiveness of sins, and his resurrection brings new life; this is the foundation and hope of our faith.

Paul points out that after his resurrection Jesus appeared many times: to Peter, to the twelve apostles, to more than five hundred brothers, then to James and all the apostles, and finally to Paul himself. These specific witnesses confirm that the resurrection was not a hallucination or a rumor, but a real event that truly happened.

Paul describes himself as “one born at the wrong time,” showing that he was unworthy to see the Lord, and had even persecuted the church, yet the risen Christ appeared to him personally and turned him from an enemy into an apostle. This is the power of the gospel: it can bring repentance and renewal, and change the whole direction of a life.
a: Be sure of the truth of the resurrection
Firmly believe that Jesus truly rose again, that he is alive today and reigns in my life.
Live out the resurrection life
No longer be ruled by sin, but be free through the Lord and live in the pattern of new life.
Become a witness
Like Paul, share your own encounter with the Lord, so that more people come to know the risen Lord.
q: Do I truly believe that the risen Jesus is with me? How has his resurrection changed the way I view life and suffering?
pr: Lord Jesus, thank You for dying on the cross for my sins and rising from the dead, giving me new life. Help me to live every day in the power of the resurrection, to boldly witness to Your reality, so that more people may gain the hope of eternal life through me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Christ is risen! He lives in my heart, and I am more than a conqueror every day!

t: Boldly Speak Up for Your Inheritance
v: Then the daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of Manasseh the son of Joseph came near. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, and before the princes and all the congregation, at the door of the Tent of Meeting, saying,
“Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the company of those who gathered themselves together against the LORD in the company of Korah, but he died in his own sin. He had no sons.
Why should the name of our father be taken away from among his family, because he had no son? Give to us a possession among the brothers of our father.”
Moses brought their cause before the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“The daughters of Zelophehad speak right. You shall surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father’s brothers. You shall cause the inheritance of their father to pass to them.
b: In an age when inheritance passed through the fathers, the five daughters of Zelophehad stepped forward boldly to claim the right to their father’s portion. They did not shrink back by saying, “We are only women,” and they did not grumble about their circumstances. They brought their petition to God’s servants with reverence and faith.

They believed that God is righteous and shows no partiality, and that the inheritance he had promised would not be lost because of their gender. Their action became a testimony of faith and courage, and it changed Israel’s law, so that when a family had no son, daughters could receive the inheritance.

God’s response to them was full of affirmation: “The daughters of Zelophehad speak right.” These words were more than a legal ruling; they were God’s praise for a group of daughters of faith. He delights to vindicate those who stand in faith and boldly seek his righteousness, and to open a way for them.
a: Stand boldly in the truth
When you face injustice or hardship, do not stay silent and passive. Stand in the promises of God with faith.
Make your request in faith
When you speak with reverence and in line with God’s heart, he will hear you and act.
Trust that God’s justice shows no partiality
God looks at faith, not status. His promises come to everyone who trusts in him.
q: Do I have the courage to stand up for God’s promises? Do I believe his justice will vindicate me and open the way for me?
pr: Lord, thank You that You value faith and not outward circumstances. Give me courage, like the daughters of Zelophehad, to stand in faith even in unjust situations and to seek Your righteousness and Your will. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God watches over me and gives me the courage to receive the inheritance that is rightfully mine in his promises!

t: Praise the King Who Reigns Forever
v: I will exalt you, my God, the King. I will praise your name forever and ever.
Every day I will praise you. I will extol your name forever and ever.
Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised! His greatness is unsearchable.
One generation will commend your works to another, and will declare your mighty acts.
I will meditate on the glorious majesty of your honor, on your wondrous works.
Men will speak of the might of your awesome acts. I will declare your greatness.
They will utter the memory of your great goodness, and will sing of your righteousness.
The LORD is gracious, merciful, slow to anger, and of great loving kindness.
The LORD is good to all. His tender mercies are over all his works.
All your works will give thanks to you, LORD. Your saints will extol you.
They will speak of the glory of your kingdom, and talk about your power,
to make known to the sons of men his mighty acts, the glory of the majesty of his kingdom.
Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom. Your dominion endures throughout all generations. The LORD is faithful in all his words, and loving in all his deeds.
b: This psalm is a song of praise that rose from the depths of David’s soul. He was not only thankful for God’s grace; he worshiped God for his eternal and boundless greatness. From “every day I will bless you” to “forever and ever,” David shows that praise is not an occasional emotion but the rhythm of life, because God’s greatness and goodness rise above time and circumstance.

The psalmist looks back on God’s wonderful works and proclaims his grace, righteousness, and loving kindness. He does not praise alone; he calls every generation to tell of what God has done, so that the world may know how glorious and everlasting his Kingdom is. It is a wave of praise that moves from personal worship to the community, and then to all peoples.

God’s Kingdom is not changed by the times and cannot be shaken by any power. His reign lasts from generation to generation. When we praise him, we realign our focus: we stop staring at the chaos of the world and look up to the King who reigns forever.
a: Let praise be your daily breath
In good times and hard times, choose to open your mouth in praise, and let God’s name be lifted high in your life.
Tell of God’s works
Do not only give thanks yourself; tell the next generation and others of God’s wonders, so that praise is passed down from age to age.
Live with the vision of God’s Kingdom
Believe that he still reigns and that his Kingdom will never be shaken, and live out the dignity and hope of a citizen of heaven here on earth.
q: Do I praise God every day with my mouth and my heart? Am I willing to let my life be a testimony that helps others know God’s glory?
pr: Lord, You are great and worthy of the highest praise. Thank You that Your love, righteousness, and faithfulness last forever. Help me respond to You with praise in every circumstance, and let my life be a witness to the glory of Your Kingdom. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will bless my King every day and let his glory be lifted high in my life forever!

t: Go Forward with the Lord’s Authority and Presence
v: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.
When they saw him, they bowed down to him; but some doubted.
Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
b: This passage is known as the Great Commission. It is the risen Lord’s final charge to his disciples and his sending of all believers. Even though some worshiped and some still doubted, Jesus called them with grace and authority: “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.” These words are the foundation of our confidence to act: it does not depend on our ability, but on the Lord’s almighty power.

“Go and make disciples of all nations” is an active call. It does not wait for an opportunity; it carries a mission into the world. The disciples’ task is not only to preach the gospel but to nurture lives, so that people come to know and obey the Lord’s word. It is a spiritual journey that begins in faith and is completed in obedience.

Finally, the Lord makes a promise: “I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” These words are the strength of everyone who serves. He not only sends us; he walks among us. Wherever we are and whatever we face, his presence is our greatest security and comfort.
a: Be sure of the Lord’s authority
Do not act in your own strength, but trust that Jesus has all authority and will bring his purposes to pass.
Live out the Lord’s mission
Actively “go” in daily life, and be a disciple’s witness at home, at work, and in your community.
Rely on the Lord’s presence
When you meet challenges or weakness, remember his promise: he is with us always.
q: Am I living out the mission the Lord has entrusted to me? Do I believe that the Lord walks with me, anytime and anywhere?
pr: Lord, thank You for giving us all authority in heaven and on earth, so that we can go in faith to fulfill Your mission. Give me courage and wisdom to proclaim Your name in daily life, to teach others to obey Your word, and to always know the peace of Your presence with me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I go forward boldly in the Lord’s authority, because he is with me to the end of the age!

t: A Woman Who Fears God Is Most Valuable
v: She makes linen garments and sells them, and delivers sashes to the merchant.
Strength and dignity are her clothing. She laughs at the time to come.
She opens her mouth with wisdom. Kind instruction is on her tongue.
She looks well to the ways of her household, and doesn’t eat the bread of idleness.
Her children rise up and call her blessed. Her husband also praises her:
“Many women do noble things, but you excel them all.”
Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain; but a woman who fears the LORD, she shall be praised.
Give her of the fruit of her hands! Let her works praise her in the gates!
b: This passage portrays a woman who fears God. She is not only diligent and wise; she has an inner spiritual strength and beauty. Her worth lies not in appearance or material success, but in making the fear of God the foundation of her life.

“Strength and dignity are her clothing” means that her character shines brighter than jewels. “She laughs at the time to come” shows her faith and hope, because she knows the future is in God’s hands. Her words are full of wisdom and kindness, and her actions are steady and fruitful. At home and in society alike she shows the dignity God gives.

A woman like this is not only pleasing to God; she is a blessing and a glory to her family. Her children are blessed because of her, and her husband is thankful for her. The world values appearance and success, but God values a heart that fears him and acts faithfully. True beauty is the wisdom and gentleness that grow out of the fear of God.
a: Make the fear of God your foundation
Outward beauty fades, but a heart that fears God makes a life glorious for the long term.
Live with wisdom and kindness
Let your words be full of grace and your actions bring blessing, so that people see God’s goodness through you.
Be faithful in managing what God has entrusted to you
At home, at work, or in ministry, give your best for God and let your life bear fruit.
q: Is the fear of God at the center of my life? Do I show wisdom, gentleness, and faithfulness in my daily life?
pr: Lord, make me a person who fears You, and show through my life the wisdom, strength, and kindness that come from You. May my life be a blessing to my family and let Your glory be seen. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I fear the LORD, and I will be a life that glorifies God and blesses others!

t: See the Risen Lord and Receive True Peace
v: Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that he had said these things to her.

When therefore it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the middle and said to them, “Peace be to you.”
When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad when they saw the Lord.
Therefore Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book;
but these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name.
b: On resurrection morning, Mary Magdalene became the first person to see the Lord. Her sorrow turned to joy because the risen Lord appeared to her himself. Her testimony was full of joy and strength: “I have seen the Lord!” This is the heart of every believer’s faith: not a religious idea, but a living Savior.

That evening the disciples were still afraid and had shut themselves in, but Jesus passed through their fear and stood among them. His first words were, “Peace be to you.” This peace is not calm circumstances; it is the assurance of the risen Lord’s presence. He showed them his nail-pierced hands and his wounded side so that they would know the One who conquered death was still with them in love and compassion.

The resurrection of Jesus is not only a historical event; it is a turning point for life. He brings people from fear into peace, and from despair into faith. His purpose, as John says, is “that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing you may have life in his name.” The life that comes through this faith is eternal, abundant, and full of joy.
a: Believe in the reality of the resurrection
Do not only know that he rose; live out, day by day, a faith in fellowship with the risen Lord.
Receive peace in the Lord
However turbulent your circumstances, Jesus still says, “Peace be to you,” because his presence is greater than all fear.
Become a witness of the resurrection
Like Mary, boldly declare, “I have seen the Lord,” so that people see the Lord’s reality and glory in you.
q: Am I truly experiencing the presence and peace of the risen Lord in my life? Am I willing to be a messenger who carries the news that the Lord is alive?
pr: Lord, thank You for rising from the dead and giving me new life in You. Place Your peace in my heart so that I am not held by fear, and give me courage to testify of Your resurrection and love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I believe Jesus is risen, and he is with me, giving me peace and a new life!

t: A Living Hope in the Midst of Trials
v: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
to an incorruptible and undefiled inheritance that doesn’t fade away, reserved in Heaven for you,
who by the power of God are guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been grieved in various trials,
that the proof of your faith, which is more precious than gold that perishes, even though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ—
whom, not having known, you love. In him, though now you don’t see him, yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy that is unspeakable and full of glory,
receiving the result of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
Therefore prepare your minds for action. Be sober, and set your hope fully on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ—
b: Peter wrote to believers who were suffering, and he reminded them that although the road of this life is hard, in Christ we already have a “living hope.” This hope is not optimism; it is rooted in the life of the risen Lord and is guaranteed by God’s own promise.

The believer’s inheritance is not of this world; it is a heavenly inheritance that is “incorruptible, undefiled, and doesn’t fade away.” Even as we go through all kinds of trials, God is refining our faith there, as gold is purified by fire. The true worth of faith is not holding on when life is easy, but trusting God when life is hard.

Peter points out that although we have never seen Jesus, we are filled with joy because we believe in him. This joy is heavenly glory and the witness of the Holy Spirit in our hearts. When the Lord returns, all our endurance, faith, and love will be turned into eternal glory and salvation.
So he urges believers to “prepare your minds for action, be sober, and set your hope fully.” True hope makes us live alert and steady. We are not crushed by reality; we hold on to the end by faith.
a: Look to the Lord in trials
Do not be knocked down by circumstances. Trials are a chance for faith to be refined and for us to become more like Christ.
Hold on to hope by faith
A living hope is not fantasy; it is the assurance that comes from God’s promises.
Be sober and wait with focus
Adjust your mindset and your focus, and let hope in the Lord’s return be the daily motivation of your life.
q: Do I still have hope in difficulty? Do I believe that God is using trials to refine my faith?
pr: Lord, thank You for the living hope You gave me through the resurrection. Help me to trust Your good purpose in trials, and to hold on to joy and faith in hope until the day I see Your glorious face. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I have hope even in trials, because the Lord is risen and his grace will keep me to the end!

t: A Humble Heart That Takes No Joy in Others’ Misfortune
v: The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high, who says in his heart, ‘Who will bring me down to the ground?’
Though you mount on high as the eagle, and though your nest is set among the stars, I will bring you down from there,” says the LORD.
“If thieves came to you, if robbers by night—oh, what disaster awaits you—wouldn’t they only steal until they had enough? If grape pickers came to you, wouldn’t they leave some gleaning grapes?
How Esau will be ransacked! How his hidden treasures are sought out!

All the men of your alliance have brought you on your way, even to the border. The men who were at peace with you have deceived you, and prevailed against you. Friends who eat your bread lay a snare under you. There is no understanding in him.”
“Won’t I in that day”, says the LORD, “destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mountain of Esau?
Your mighty men, Teman, will be dismayed, to the end that everyone may be cut off from the mountain of Esau by slaughter.
But don’t look down on your brother in the day of his disaster, and don’t rejoice over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction. Don’t speak proudly in the day of distress.
Don’t enter into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity. Don’t look down on their affliction in the day of their calamity, neither seize their wealth on the day of their calamity.
b: Obadiah’s message is a warning to Edom. In their pride they deceived themselves, thinking that the high mountains and strong terrain would protect them, and forgetting that God is the Most High. When people rely on their position, wisdom, or alliances, they fall into the illusion that they can never be shaken. But God says, “Though you mount on high as the eagle, I will bring you down from there.”

Edom’s sin was not only pride but also coldness toward their brother. When Judah was in trouble they stood by, even gloating and kicking them while they were down. This reminds us that when others suffer, to hold them in contempt or judge them is to take part in the harm. God’s eyes see everything. He will vindicate the suffering, and he will judge the proud and indifferent.

True wisdom is not protecting ourselves but having a humble heart and loving others. God delights in a humble and merciful heart, and hates arrogance and self-righteousness. May we learn not to rejoice over others’ failures or criticize their weaknesses, but to have compassion, pray for them, and support them. That is a heart that pleases God.
a: Be alert to a proud heart
Do not rely on your own strength or status. Remember that all stability is in God.
Replace indifference with love
When others are in trouble, do not stand by or judge; choose to reach out and pray.
Have a humble, merciful heart
See people with God’s eyes and respond with grace, so that we build one another up in love.
q: Have I ever felt pride or indifference when someone else failed? When people around me are in difficulty, am I willing to be the one who reaches out to support them?
pr: Lord, remove all pride and indifference from my heart, so that I do not look down on anyone. Teach me to reach out a merciful hand when others suffer, and to fulfill Your will in love. May all my conduct show Your grace and humility. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will have a humble and merciful heart, replace indifference with love, and walk in the way that pleases God!

t: Renewed Strength in the Lord’s Mercy
v: It is because of the LORD’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his mercies don’t fail.
They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
“The LORD is my portion,” says my soul. “Therefore I will hope in him.”
The LORD is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him.
It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD.
It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.
Let him sit alone and keep silence, because he has laid it on him.
Let him put his mouth in the dust, if it is so that there may be hope.
Let him give his cheek to him who strikes him. Let him be filled full of reproach.
For the Lord will not cast off forever.
For though he causes grief, yet he will have compassion according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
For he does not afflict willingly, nor grieve the children of men.
